subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood inference fit for Nova Analytics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nova-analytics.com>
Cc: Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@nova-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood inference fit for Nova Analytics

Hi Tom / Jane,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the candid discussion about Nova's inference needs. Quick recap from my side and a proposed next step: 

- Key pain: inconsistent latency across peak inference workloads, rising per-token cost, and lack of a unified rollout strategy for model updates.
- What we demo'd: Redwood Dedicated routing + prefix caching, cost/latency dashboards, and canary rollouts for model updates.
- Preliminary fit: strong match for your product team (predictable latency + rollout controls) and potential cost savings with prefix/KV caching on your historical query patterns.

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical review with your ML infra lead to map current inference pipeline (model sizes, sequence lengths, burst patterns) and estimate unit economics. I can loop in Neha from our onboarding team for capacity sizing if that sounds good.

Attachments: 20270410-Discovery-Notes.pdf (call notes), Redwood-RoI-model-spec.pdf (example cost model template)

Availability: I have Tues/Wed next week (4/13-4/14) in the morning PST. If that doesn't work, send a couple slots and I'll book.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0192

On Fri, Apr 9, 2027 at 10:20 AM Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nova-analytics.com> wrote:

> 
> -Tom

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nova-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@nova-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood inference fit for Nova Analytics

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap — Alex wasn't available this morning but Jane and I reviewed the notes. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we schedule the technical review:

1) For prefix caching, do you have a recommended minimum request volume to see meaningful savings?
2) Any integrations required on our side for the tracing hooks? We use an internal tracing pipeline (OpenTelemetry) and want to make sure it plugs in cleanly.

If you can send short answers to those two, we can pull Alex in next week.

Best,
Tom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nova-analytics.com>
Cc: Jane Roberts <jane.roberts@nova-analytics.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood inference fit for Nova Analytics

Hi Tom — quick answers: 

1) Minimum volume: You typically start seeing measurable ROI once you have ~200 requests/day with repeat prefixes across sessions; with heavy repeat conversational prefixes the breakeven can be much lower. Neha (cc'd) can run a modeled example off a sample qps distribution if you can share anonymized logs.

2) Tracing: Redwood exposes OTEL-compatible hooks. Most customers wire a lightweight agent on the sidecar or use our ingest endpoint; we don't require deep changes to your pipeline. We'll include a short integration checklist in the technical review.

If next week looks good for Alex, send a couple slots and I'll get Neha to lead capacity modeling.

—Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nova-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: Bump: Technical review + quick integration checklist

Hi Tom — just bumping this thread in case it slipped through. We haven't locked a time with Alex yet; still happy to run a 30-min technical review and walk through a quick integration checklist and a rough cost model using a few of your anonymized samples.

If priorities have shifted, quick note on timing helps — happy to push to next quarter or set a short async review.

If helpful, here's a one-click slot to book: https://calendly.com/marissa-cole/redwood-demo

Thanks — Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nova-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick pulse — fit / priority for Redwood?

Hi Tom — following up one more time. I wanted to check two quick things: 

1) Is Redwood still on the evaluation shortlist for this quarter?
2) If not, is there a better timeframe to reconnect (e.g., Q3 planning)?

If it's not a fit right now, no worries — a one-line reply is totally fine and I'll update our pipeline. If it is, I'm happy to run a short async assessment from a sample of 1k queries (anonymized) and return a 1-page cost/latency delta within 72 hours.

Thanks again — Marissa
